finding.title: Remove stray .gitkeep placeholder files from non-empty lib/ directories
finding.why: .gitkeep files exist only to make git track an otherwise-empty directory. lib/core/constants/ has held 3 real source files this whole time, so this .gitkeep serves no purpose. An informal repo-wide grep (context only, not a full audit) found the same stale pattern in roughly 103 other lib/ directories, e.g. core/database/daos/.gitkeep sitting alongside 48 real files — almost certainly leftover from an initial scaffold generator never cleaned up once real files landed. Zero functional risk; it's noise in `git status`/`find` output and a minor signal that scaffold cleanup isn't part of the standard workflow.
finding.recommendation: Delete .gitkeep from any lib/ directory that already contains another tracked file; keep it only where a directory is genuinely still empty.
acceptance_criteria: A `make audit` (or pre-commit) check flags any .gitkeep whose directory contains another tracked file

finding.title: Relocate test/core/streak/*_test.dart to mirror lib/features/gamification/streak/ (AG-5)
finding.why: Commit 92125f82 ('refactor(W2.22): promote core/streak/ -> features/gamification/streak/', 20 May 2026) moved all 5 streak source files out of core/, but left both test files behind at test/core/streak/. AG-5 requires lib/a/b/foo.dart <-> test/a/b/foo_test.dart. A contributor working on lib/features/gamification/streak/ who checks test/features/gamification/streak/ (as AG-5 promises) finds nothing, risking duplicate tests or a false 'no coverage' assumption for a module that actually has 305 lines of tests, including two named D17 regression tests.
finding.recommendation: git mv both files to test/features/gamification/streak/{streak_event_test.dart,streak_state_provider_test.dart}. Note the new location is one directory level deeper, so streak_state_provider_test.dart's helper import must change from '../../helpers/drift_memory.dart' to '../../../helpers/drift_memory.dart'. Verify `flutter test test/features/gamification/streak/` is green and delete the now-empty test/core/streak/ dir.
acceptance_criteria: test/core/streak/ no longer exists; both suites pass unchanged at test/features/gamification/streak/.
The [Pending] AG-5 unmirrored-test-file audit check referenced at docs/coding-standards.md:523, once implemented, reports zero violations for this module.

finding.title: Assert the actual zero value, not just non-emptiness, in streak_state_provider_test.dart's 'stream emits new value' test

evidence.quote:
await Future<void>.delayed(Duration.zero);
      expect(states, isNotEmpty); // zero at start

finding.why: The comment states the intent ('zero at start') but `expect(states, isNotEmpty)` only proves an emission arrived, not that its value is 0 -- a regression that made the initial computed streak nonzero (e.g. a restore/reduce ordering bug) would still pass this line. In practice the invariant IS protected elsewhere in the same file ('emits streak state as a stream' and 'emits empty state when no events', lines 131-141, both assert currentStreak==0 on first emission), so this specific line just doesn't pull its own weight and its comment overclaims what it checks.
acceptance_criteria: Assertion at streak_state_provider_test.dart:166 checks the emitted value equals 0, matching its own comment.

finding.title: Pin StreakStateProvider's day-bucketing seam instead of letting streak_state_provider_test.dart depend on the host machine's timezone
finding.why: read()/watch() call StreakReducer.reduce() without pinning the injectable `dayOf` seam that streak_reducer.dart's own doc comment says exists precisely 'so tests can pin a fixed UTC offset deterministically without depending on the host machine's timezone.' Both FakeLocalDayClock.today() and the default dayOf (DateUtils.extractLocalDate, date_utils.dart:64) resolve through DateTime.toLocal(), which reads the executing machine's TZ -- confirmed empirically inside the real flutter_tester harness: `TZ=Pacific/Kiritimati flutter test` shows DateTime.utc(2026,5,14,12).toLocal() shift a full calendar day. I could not flip any assertion in this specific file under that TZ (ran the suite 3x under the sandbox default Europe/London and once under forced Pacific/Kiritimati, all 13 tests green each time) because every fixture here sits at hour 0 or hour 12 UTC and every current day-gap still lands inside the reducer's +/-1-day grace window either way -- that is a property of today's specific fixture values, not a guarantee. The sibling unit suite (test/features/sync/domain/reducers/streak_reducer_test.dart:120-158) already tests the local-vs-UTC distinction correctly by injecting dayOf directly; this integration-level file has no such seam and inherits toLocal()'s host dependency instead. A fixture pair whose UTC-hour asymmetry straddles a day boundary differently under some real TZ (e.g. clock seeded at 23:00 UTC, event at 01:00 UTC) would confirm an actual flip -- the D17 rollover test already seeds close to a boundary and is the most likely one to trip this by accident in a future edit.
finding.recommendation: Either give StreakStateProvider.read/watch an explicit dayOf override (mirroring the reducer's own seam) or have the test suite pin TZ=UTC explicitly (Makefile/CI env var) so pass/fail can't depend on the runner's locale.
acceptance_criteria: `TZ=Pacific/Kiritimati flutter test test/core/streak/streak_state_provider_test.dart` and the default-TZ run both stay green by construction (pinned dayOf or pinned TZ), not by coincidence of current fixture values.

finding.title: Rename the domain StreakEvent so it stops colliding with Drift's generated StreakEvent row class

evidence.quote: class StreakEvent extends DataClass implements Insertable<StreakEvent> {

finding.why: Two unrelated public top-level classes share the name StreakEvent: the hand-written domain value type that streak_event_test.dart exercises, and Drift's generated row class. It's self-aware (the domain class's own doc comment explains the collision) and worked around with `hide StreakEvent` at the one call site needing both today, but every future file that needs both the Drift row and the domain value is one missing hide/alias away from a confusing 'wrong StreakEvent' type error, and the name can't be used unqualified in review comments, Linear tickets, or docs.
finding.recommendation: Rename the domain class (e.g. StreakLogEvent) -- it's the smaller of the two and all its call sites are internal to the streak feature.
acceptance_criteria: `grep -rn 'class StreakEvent' learning_tracker/lib/` returns exactly one hand-written match plus the Drift-generated one, under distinguishable names.
